successCriteria.description: Create src/modules/policy/policy.model.ts with LeavePolicy interface containing all specified fields: id, policyName, leaveType (imported from src/shared/types/leave.types.ts), entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, allowNegativeBalance, maxConsecutiveDays, fiscalYear, createdAt, updatedAt
Create src/modules/policy/policy.repository.ts with ILeavePolicyRepository interface defining: findById, findByLeaveType, findActivePolicies, create, update, delete
Implement LeavePolicyRepository class implementing ILeavePolicyRepository using the pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts
Include Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/policy/ covering the model and repository

constraints: All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001) — the LeavePolicyRepository must use the pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts; no inline SQL outside the repository class
LeaveType must be imported from the canonical location src/shared/types/leave.types.ts — do not redefine or duplicate the enum
No `any` types — use `unknown` with type guards where needed (HARNESS.json constraint: no-any)
Strict TypeScript: no implicit any, strict null checks — all fields must have explicit types
Repository interface method signatures are contracts for later phases (Phase 5 service, Phase 8 routes) — they must be complete and unambiguous
outOfScope: LeavePolicy service layer (ILeavePolicyService interface and LeavePolicyService class) — deferred to Phase 5
LeavePolicy Fastify routes and barrel export index.ts — deferred to Phase 8
Audit record emission (GP-002) from repository state-changing operations — not specified for this phase; will be handled at the service layer in Phase 5
Database migrations / Knex schema for the leave_policies table — this phase only defines the model interface and repository, not the DDL
Integration tests — only unit tests are required for this phase; integration tests are deferred to Phase 8

ambiguities.description: The `id` field type on LeavePolicy is not specified — could be `number` (serial), `string` (UUID), or another type. This affects all repository method signatures (findById, update, delete) and downstream consumers.

The `LeavePolicyQueryParams` DTO has no fields specified in the intent. It is unclear which query parameters should be supported (e.g., filtering by leaveType, isActive, fiscalYear; pagination; sorting).
options: Full filter DTO mirroring all queryable fields

ambiguities.description: The `create` method input type is not specified — could be `Omit<LeavePolicy, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>`, a separate `CreateLeavePolicyDto`, or `Partial<LeavePolicy>`. This affects the repository contract.
options: Partial<LeavePolicy> with required fields enforced at runtime

ambiguities.description: The `update` method input type is not specified — could be `Partial<LeavePolicy>` (partial update) or a full `LeavePolicy` (full replacement). This affects the repository contract and how callers use it.
The `fiscalYear` field type is not specified — could be `number` (e.g., 2024) or `string` (e.g., '2024' or 'FY2024'). This affects query parameter design and database column type.

The `createdAt` and `updatedAt` field types are not specified — could be `Date` objects or ISO 8601 `string` values. This affects serialization and how the repository returns these fields from PostgreSQL.
